title: Vademecum of the GPAI Signatory Taskforce

policy_extraction.issuing_body: European AI Office / Signatory Taskforce of the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
covered_actors: Signatories to the GPAI Code of Practice

evidence.quote: to facilitate cooperation between Signatories where relevant for the purpose of implementing the Code
The Taskforce may adopt outputs relating to its Objectives under Point 2 by consensus based on all Members
The AI Office may publish this Vademecum, the list of organisations participating in any meeting, and the high-level minutes of meetings as required by its transparency obligations
The Taskforce is chaired by the AI Office
Meetings of the Taskforce shall be convened by the AI Office either on its own initiative or at the request of a simple majority of the Members

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This Vademecum governs the internal organisation and operation of the Signatory Taskforce under the GPAI Code of Practice, which was assessed as adequate pursuant to Article 56(6) of the AI Act. It is not itself a binding instrument but structures voluntary cooperation among signatories. The AI Office chairs the Taskforce and may publish the Vademecum, participant lists, and high-level meeting minutes under its transparency obligations. Decisions are taken by consensus with a default agreement period of no less than 10 working days.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document is primarily procedural, establishing the governance structure of a Signatory Taskforce for the GPAI Code of Practice under the EU AI Act. The dominant framing is innovation enablement — the taskforce exists to facilitate cooperative implementation of the Code, exchange views on technological developments, and adapt guidance to market and technological changes. Safety and rights concerns appear implicitly through references to the 'risk landscape' and 'societal developments,' but are secondary to enabling structured industry participation and code compliance.

evidence_spans.quote: to provide input on guidance documents produced by the AI Office that are relevant to the Code, in view of technological, societal, market, and legislative developments

to exchange views on technological developments, changes in the risk landscape, or experience with the application of the AI Act rules that could be relevant for potential future reviews or updates of the Code
seeking and discussing research, independent expert input, and up-to-date evidence relevant to the Code's commitments or measures, such as emerging practices
